title: Stochastic Thermodynamics on Time-Evolving Curved Spaces
authors: Rihito Nagase, Shoki Sugimoto, Asuka Takatsu, Takahiro Sagawa
abstract: We construct stochastic thermodynamics of overdamped Langevin systems on nonrelaticvistic curved spaces with time-dependent metrics. The time dependence of the metric contributes to the energy balance by performing work on the kinetic energy, which is instantaneously dissipated as heat in the overdamped regime. This contribution makes our framework thermodynamically consistent so that entropy production satisfies the second law of thermodynamics. As a special case, when the metric evolves according to backward Ricci flow, the entropy balance exhibits a structure similar to Perelman's entropy functional. Our framework provides a way to quantify thermodynamic costs in dynamics on time-evolving spaces such as diffusion on membranes.
summary: This paper develops stochastic thermodynamics for systems moving on curved spaces whose metrics change with time. It introduces a crucial correction term ($\dot{G}_t$) into the energy balance equations to ensure that entropy production always obeys the Second Law, even when geometry changes. This framework is vital for quantifying thermodynamic costs in dynamic physical settings like diffusion on evolving membranes.
main_problem: The core problem is constructing a thermodynamically consistent framework for stochastic thermodynamics when the underlying physical space has a time-dependent metric.
main_result: The authors derive necessary correction terms ($\dot{G}_t$) to the standard heat and work definitions, ensuring that the total entropy production rate rigorously satisfies the Second Law of Thermodynamics even as the geometry evolves.
method: The methodology involves analyzing energy balance using overdamped Langevin dynamics on curved manifolds, employing relative entropy calculations between forward and backward processes in the $\epsilon 	o 0$ limit.
model_or_system: The system is an overdamped Langevin process evolving on a nonrelativistic curved space described by a time-dependent metric $g_t$. The analysis uses Fokker-Planck equations and concepts from geometric measure theory.
key_observables: Entropy production rate ($\dot{\Sigma}_t$), Heat rate ($\dot{Q}_t$), Work rate ($\dot{W}_t$), and the metric correction term ($\dot{G}_t$).
important_parameters: The time dependence of the metric ($g_t$) is crucial, as are the overdamped regime assumption and the small noise limit ($\epsilon 	o 0$).
main_assumptions: Assumes the topology remains constant (diffeomorphic) and that the heat bath thermalizes much faster than the manifold evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of $\dot{Q}_t$, $\dot{W}_t$, and $\dot{G}_t$ for a sphere example, comparing correct non-negative entropy production against naive calculations that violate the Second Law.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the dynamics on curved spaces to establishing detailed balance conditions via relative entropy measures. It then derives the full thermodynamic decomposition of energy change, culminating in showing the dynamics are a gradient flow of the relative entropy functional under a Wasserstein metric.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful tools for analyzing non-equilibrium processes where the environment or geometry itself is changing over time, which is relevant for understanding open quantum systems coupled to dynamic baths or evolving media.
